chunks: From him, and from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the drowned person: should he be given ghusl? He said, “Yes, he is given ghusl and his condition is to be ascertained.” I said, “And how is his condition ascertained?” He said, “He is left for three days before he is buried, unless he changes beforehand, in which case he is given ghusl and buried. And likewise the one struck by lightning, for it may sometimes be thought that he has died while he has not died.”

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: a period of three days before burial
key_terms.يُسْتَبْرَأُ: his state is verified to ensure death has truly occurred
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: he is given ghusl for the dead

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing and burying a drowned person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who appears to have died by drowning or lightning strike. It states that such a person is to be given ghusl, but burial may be delayed for three days to verify death unless bodily change appears sooner, in which case burial proceeds.
